cards.body: This week traced one of the most emotionally rich arcs in your Life Map: a perfect Tokyo night at Golden Gai, a first-class flight into Bora Bora, and then — mid-lagoon, mid-vacation — a quiet realization that shifted everything. You kept building Gremly (4 DCO features shipped from a poolside cabana), but by March 12 you named what mattered more: 'I need to step back sometimes and just enjoy him.' That's new. Prior weeks showed anxiety about not moving fast enough. This week showed you choosing.
cards.quote: Realizing that even though I love Gremly work, I need to step back sometimes and just enjoy him and being on a once in a lifetime vacation.
cards.headline: Japan concluded, Bora Bora bloomed, and you chose presence

moments.body: Golden Gai is one of Tokyo's most singular places — a warren of 200 tiny bars in Shinjuku, each seating maybe eight people, preserved since the 1970s. You hit it after a Michelin-star dinner, then Shibuya Crossing, an arcade, an onsen, and a sake tasting where you ended up drinking with a high-ranking member of the Japanese Air Defense. That's not a tourist itinerary — that's a perfect night. The kind you'll describe for years.
moments.title: A Perfect Night in Tokyo

moments.body: Tennis with Dave. A run. Weights. No alcohol. Three Gremly todos shipped. And you woke up feeling 'very very refreshed' after a long sleep in Bora Bora. You asked yourself whether the sleep made the difference — it probably did. This was the week's clearest proof that rest isn't the enemy of productivity; it's the engine. One of the fullest single days in your recent data.
moments.title: The Day You Had It All

spotlight.title: The shift from guilt-driven to joy-driven work
spotlight.takeaway: You didn't stop building Gremly on vacation — you stopped feeling bad about the pace. That's a different thing entirely, and it showed up in your output.
spotlight.evidence_trail: Feb 27: 'can't help but feel like I'm not moving quick enough with the app.' Feb 26: 'Feeling guilty I'm not putting more into actual work.' Then: March 8 in Bora Bora — you completed 3 DCO todos and wrote about it with pride, not anxiety. March 9: 3 more todos completed, 3 new ones created. March 12: 'I need to step back sometimes and just enjoy him' — a conscious choice, not a collapse. March 13: you completed 'DCO Implementation Across Areas' and wrote your most purely grateful journal entry of the entire dataset. The work continued. The guilt didn't.

research_context.body: Psychological research on intrinsic vs. extrinsic motivation shows that when people shift from 'I must do this' to 'I want to do this,' creative output often improves even as hours decrease. The anxiety of 'not moving fast enough' is a form of self-imposed pressure that can paradoxically slow progress. Vacation — especially one with genuine presence and recovery sleep — can reset that pressure valve, allowing the same work to feel energizing rather than depleting.

cards.body: The first week of March captured a before-and-after: the anxious, depleted founder who shipped TestFlight on February 26 became someone floating on a lagoon in Bora Bora, genuinely choosing presence over productivity. Work didn't disappear — Gremly kept moving — but the relationship to it changed. The one thread that didn't follow the upward arc is running, which will define the final days of March.
cards.headline: March opened mid-honeymoon and immediately became the most emotionally rich month in your recent data.

thread_arcs.arc: Arrived in Tokyo Feb 27, peaked with a perfect Golden Gai night, and concluded March 6 with 'incredible' as the final word.
Every journal entry in March mentions Dave — the month has been a sustained, documented deepening of the relationship across three countries.
TestFlight shipped the last day of February; March opened with the DCO feature sprint — 4 completions from vacation — marking the shift from launch anxiety to post-launch iteration confidence.
The half marathon goal set in January now has a race date (March 22) but not enough training miles — the month's biggest unresolved tension.
February closed with anxiety and guilt; March opened with gratitude and presence — the habit rate improved from ~31% to 43% and the journal tone shifted completely.
